messages:
maria: Spawning a follow-up thread on a different tack: instead of a hard uncertainty threshold for fallbacks, what if we use a per-route stochastic fallback budget driven by token/sequence entropy? Means low-bit responses emit an `entropy_score` and a route-level budget decides probabilistic reruns to control cost/quality tradeoffs. Thoughts?

devon: interesting. So we’d sample higher-entropy responses more often for rerun, keeping overall fallback rate bounded. How do we compute `entropy_score` cheaply?

maria: two parts: fast LM-token-entropy (cheap, from next-token logits) and a downstream calibrated sequence-entropy aggregate. runtime emits both: `{e_token:0.92, e_seq:0.71, model_sig: 'm45-2026-03'}`.

liam: budget mechanics: each route has `budget = B per 1k requests`. When a response arrives we compute P(rerun) = f(entropy, budget_remaining). Option: P = min(1, entropy / K) * (budget_remaining / expected_remaining). Need a stable schedule to avoid bursts.

jules: are we okay with non-deterministic behavior for customers? some customers expect deterministic responses for same prompt.

maria: deterministic paths unaffected. stochastic fallback only enabled for routes opting into low-bit aggressive cost controls. We add explicit flag `fallback_mode=stochastic` in route config or header.

ana: naming nit: use `entropy_score` rather than `e_seq` in public API. clients might want the raw numbers for their own sampling.

priyanka: telemetry implications: we need counters `entropy_bucket`, `stochastic_reruns`, `budget_spent`, `budget_refill_events`. Also trace annotations when rerun chosen vs when declined. Console needs an estimated cost-saved metric.

liam: safety: must bound worst-case cost. Do we enforce budget at the tenant level? otherwise a rogue route could exhaust cluster capacity.

maria: yes, multi-level budgets: global (per-cluster pool), tenant, and route. Route budgets borrow from tenant, tenant from global. Borrowing has configurable caps.

jules: UX: how does client request a higher confidence rerun synchronously? header `X-Redwood-Fallback: force=high_precision` would request immediate rerun and incur billed delta. Otherwise stochastic works behind the scenes.

devon: runtime changes: for each low-bit response we attach `meta: {entropy_score:0.71, rerun_prob:0.18, budget_token: 'r:12345:t:67890'}`. Budget tokens allow control plane to reconcile decisions with billing.

liam: what about streaming? rerun decision might happen after some tokens. Option A: decide only at final commit to keep logic simple. Option B: sliding-window entropy and mid-stream speculative rerun. I vote A for initial rollout.

maria: agree A. later explore tokenwise speculative rerun for latency-sensitive use-cases.

jules: evaluation matrix: measure quality lift per rerun (delta_score), wasted reruns (no uplift), tail-latency increase, and cost per effective-lift. Use held-out prompts per-tenant for accurate numbers.

ana: per-tenant calibration: capture relationship between entropy_score and expected quality delta. store tiny calibration curves `calib_id` per-tenant so routes can bias sampling more intelligently.

priyanka: billing: when a rerun happens we should emit a `rerun_event` that includes original precision and fallback precision and charge the difference. For stochastic samples we need to attribute cost to the route owner. Also expose a `budget_alert` when spend velocity exceeds threshold.

maria: security: to prevent clients from abusing `force=high_precision`, force requires an entitlement and will be rate limited and audited. Non-privileged clients get 429 when they exceed their personal fallback quota.

devon: API: propose header `X-Redwood-Fallback-Mode: stochastic;budget=50/1000;seed=42` or a JSON `policy` in the request body for richer controls. seed allows deterministic sampling for debug.

liam: deploy plan: 1) implement entropy emission in canary low-bit runtime 2) shadow stochastic sampling decisions for 2w and collect metrics 3) enable soft-stochastic (no reruns, just simulated) for 1w on subset of customers 4) enable real stochastic reruns with strict tenant budgets 5) expand.

jules: rollback criteria: 1) unexplained cost delta > 12% 2) false-negative induced quality drop measured by tests 3) fallback-induced p99 latency > SLA.

ana: metrics definitions: `stochastic_rerun_rate = reruns / requests`, `useful_rerun_rate = reruns_with_quality_delta>delta0 / reruns`, `cost_efficiency = quality_delta / extra_cost`.

priyanka: operational tasks: add budget store (redis-backed), reconcile job that consumes budget_tokens and writes billing entries, alerting playbooks for budget exhaustion. Also UI for customers to set budgets and view spend.

infra-bot: created infra task INF-4301 (budget store proto) and billing task INF-4302 (rerun reconciliation).

maria: action items: I'll draft an RFC addendum describing entropy_score definition, budget contract, API headers, telemetry keys, and rollout playbook. assign reviewers @devon @priyanka.

devon: I'll prototype entropy extraction in the fast-path runtime and a small simulator to tune K and sampling functions.

liam: I'll wire evaluation harness to compute `useful_rerun_rate` and run per-tenant slices.

priyanka: I'll own telemetry and billing hooks and add console widgets for live budget and rerun charts.

maria: thanks all. goal: two-week PoC then canary.

infra-bot: INF-4301 assigned to infra team, INF-4302 added to billing backlog.
